summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 gap closure execution (plan 23-08: Windows WinFsp extraction to crate), then run a security review of the Rust SDK extraction code and fix identified vulnerabilities.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 fully completed with all 8 plans executed and bookkeeping committed. Security review identified 2 HIGH findings; both were fixed (ed25519-dalek zeroize feature enabled, generate_ed25519_keypair return type hardened). Dead code removed from fuse crate operations files.

repo: Phase 23 is the 'rust-sdk-extraction' phase — moved WinFsp operations from desktop app into cipherbox-fuse crate, fixing a latent compile error where `pub mod windows` had no backing directory.
All KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields already use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> — the project has a consistent zeroization pattern for stored keys, but the generation path had a gap.

The fuse crate has separate platform implementations for macOS/Linux (src/operations.rs, src/write_ops.rs) and Windows (src/platform/windows/), and both must be updated in parallel for any shared logic changes.
generate_ed25519_keypair callers were wrapping the plain Vec<u8> return in redundant Zeroizing::new() — this pattern indicated awareness of the gap that the fix closes.
ed25519-dalek SigningKey does NOT zero on drop unless the 'zeroize' feature is explicitly enabled in workspace Cargo.toml.
The fuse crate uses a spawn_metadata_publish / build_folder_metadata pattern that extracts Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to plain Vec<u8> for passing to metadata publishing — this is an intentional boundary.

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair previously returned bare Vec<u8> for the private key; changed to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to ensure memory is zeroed on drop.
ed25519-dalek workspace dependency was missing the 'zeroize' feature flag; without it, SigningKey does not zero private key material on drop.

Callers of generate_ed25519_keypair were wrapping return value in Zeroizing::new(...clone()); simplified after return type change. Line 522: try_into() on Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> requires .into_inner() first since Zeroizing doesn't implement TryInto<[u8;32]>.
Same try_into() pattern as macOS path — Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> cannot be directly converted with try_into(); must call .into_inner() to extract the Vec<u8> first.
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code — resolve_file_pointers_blocking only called internally, fetch_and_populate_folder had no external callers. Both removed.
Parallel dead code copies of fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking existed in the Windows operations file; also removed.

workflow: When a GSD subagent disconnects mid-execution, spot-checking git log for phase-plan commits and verifying acceptance criteria allows safe resumption from the bookkeeping step without re-running code changes.
After a Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> return type change, callers using .try_into() to convert to [u8;32] need .into_inner() since Zeroizing doesn't implement TryInto for fixed arrays.
Dead code removal can be bundled into a security fix PR rather than deferred — the compiler warnings serve as the inventory.

friction: 1Password SSH agent failed signing 3 consecutive times mid-session, requiring user to manually unblock before the bookkeeping commit could proceed.
The GSD executor subagent disconnected with a ConnectionRefused API error after being spawned, requiring manual resumption and verification of what had already been committed.

Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> doesn't implement TryInto<[u8;32]>, requiring an into_inner() unwrap that isn't immediately obvious — discovered by tracing the try_into() call sites after changing the return type.
open_items: file_ipns_private_key in crates/fuse/src/write_ops.rs (~line 174) generates an Ed25519 key via ed25519_dalek directly (not through generate_ed25519_keypair) and returns a plain Vec<u8> — same zeroization gap exists but was noted as out of scope for this fix.
AES-CTR decryption relies on IPFS CID for integrity but the client doesn't verify the CID after fetching bytes — a HIGH finding in the security review that was not addressed in this session.
~30 generated test case suggestions in .planning/security/REVIEW-2026-03-24-phase23.md covering AES-GCM, AES-CTR, ECIES, HKDF, Ed25519, and VaultBlob are unimplemented.

build_folder_metadata / spawn_metadata_publish extracts Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to plain Vec<u8> for passing to metadata publishing — this boundary was noted but not evaluated for whether it should also use Zeroizing.
